name: modify_ldt
synopsis: int syscall(SYS_modify_ldt, int func, void *ptr, unsigned long bytecount);
Note: glibc provides no wrapper for modify_ldt(), necessitating the use of syscall(2).
description: modify_ldt() reads or writes the local descriptor table (LDT) for a process, which is an array of segment descriptors referenced by user code. Depending on the func parameter, it either reads the LDT into memory or modifies an LDT entry using a user_desc structure.

parameters.name: func
parameters.description: Function code: 0 to read the LDT, 1 or 0x11 to modify an LDT entry, or 2 for a legacy operation.

parameters.name: ptr
parameters.description: Pointer to the memory buffer for reading or writing LDT data, or to a user_desc structure for modifications.

parameters.name: bytecount
parameters.description: Number of bytes to read or write; for modifications, it must equal the size of the user_desc structure when func is 1 or 0x11.

return_value.success: Returns the actual number of bytes read (for reading) or 0 (for writing)
return_value.failure: Returns -1 and sets errno to indicate the error

errors.description: ptr points outside the address space.
ptr is 0, or func is 1 and bytecount is not equal to the size of user_desc, or func is 1 or 0x11 and the new LDT entry has invalid values.

bugs: On 64-bit kernels before Linux 3.19, setting the "lm" bit in user_desc prevents the descriptor from being considered empty, even though it does not create a long mode segment.
